skill.name: python-packaging
skill.description: Build and publish Python packages using modern pyproject.toml layouts, metadata, CLI entry points, wheels, TestPyPI, and PyPI release workflows.
skill.summary: Guide packaging structure, metadata, builds, and publication for Python libraries and CLI tools.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline paths, example URLs, and packaging commands. The .pypirc token example is a real sensitive-credential handling risk, but I found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious automation.

remediation.issue: The .pypirc example encourages storing PyPI API tokens in a home directory dotfile.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer PyPI trusted publishing or environment variables. If .pypirc is shown, require restrictive permissions and placeholder-only examples.

remediation.issue: Private index examples can be copied without trust checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to use only approved organization indexes and avoid untrusted extra-index-url fallbacks.

content.value_statement: Python packaging has many layout, metadata, build, and release choices. This skill guides project structure, package metadata, builds, TestPyPI checks, and PyPI publication.
actual_capabilities: Designs source-layout and flat-layout Python package structures.
Drafts pyproject.toml metadata for setuptools, hatchling, flit, and poetry workflows.
Explains CLI entry points using Click or argparse.
Outlines local build, wheel, source distribution, and twine check steps.
Describes TestPyPI, PyPI, private index, and GitHub Actions publishing patterns.
Provides packaging checklists, README sections, MANIFEST guidance, and versioning patterns.
limitations: It is documentation guidance and does not validate a live package repository by itself.
Publishing steps still require user-owned PyPI credentials or trusted publishing setup.
Private package index examples must be adapted to an approved organization repository.
Dependency and classifier choices need review for each project and Python support policy.

use_cases.title: Prepare a library for PyPI
use_cases.description: Create package structure, metadata, build settings, and release checks for a reusable Python library.

use_cases.title: Package a command-line tool
use_cases.description: Add entry points, CLI examples, dependencies, and installation guidance for a Python command-line application.

use_cases.title: Standardize release workflows
use_cases.description: Document build, TestPyPI, wheel, and GitHub Actions patterns for repeatable Python package releases.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me package a Python library named <name>. Recommend a file structure, core metadata, and first release checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Add CLI Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my Python script into an installable CLI package. Include entry point guidance, dependencies, tests, and build steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for PyPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my package plan for PyPI release. Check metadata, README needs, wheel builds, TestPyPI steps, and publishing risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Distribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design packaging for a multi-package Python project. Cover namespace packages, dynamic versioning, private indexes, and automated publishing.

output_examples.input: I need to publish my first Python library.
output_examples.output: A source-layout package plan with required files, metadata fields, build commands, TestPyPI validation, and a release checklist.

output_examples.input: I want users to install my tool and run one command.
output_examples.output: A CLI packaging plan with entry point naming, dependency guidance, local install checks, and documentation sections.

output_examples.input: Our team needs repeatable package releases.
output_examples.output: A release workflow outline covering versioning, wheel builds, artifact checks, PyPI publishing, and CI automation responsibilities.

best_practices: Use source layout and modern pyproject.toml metadata for distributable packages.
Build and test packages in a clean environment before publishing.
Use TestPyPI or trusted publishing workflows before a production PyPI release.
anti_patterns: Publishing without testing installation from the built wheel or source distribution.
Storing real package tokens in shared files, examples, or repository history.
Using private indexes without documenting trust boundaries and fallback behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill build packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides packaging guidance, templates, and release steps that a user or agent can apply.

faq.question: Does it support pyproject.toml?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on modern pyproject.toml workflows and includes setuptools, hatchling, flit, and poetry patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with CLI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers entry points, Click examples, argparse examples, and installation checks for command-line tools.

faq.question: Can it publish to PyPI?
faq.answer: It describes PyPI and TestPyPI steps. Users must provide approved credentials or trusted publishing configuration.

faq.question: Does it cover private package indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes private index examples that should be adapted to trusted organization repositories.

faq.question: What should users review before release?
faq.answer: Review metadata, license files, README content, tests, build artifacts, dependencies, and credential handling.
